The term “El Nino” has dominated headlines in recent weeks as much of the world struggles to cope with extreme weather.

US meteorologists announced the return of the phenomenon earlier this summer, warning it could contribute to record global temperatures and the hottest year ever recorded in 2027.

Here the Independent examines what El Nino is, how it interacts with human-driven climate change, and how it is currently affecting weather conditions across the UK.

What is El Nino?

El Nino – which means “little boy” in Spanish – is widely used to describe the warming of sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean that occurs every few years.

The phenomenon typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts several months.

open image in gallery A view of dry soil in Honduras caused by the El Nino affect. ( AFP/Getty )

It disrupts weather patterns worldwide and pushes up global temperatures.

The name comes from South American fishermen centuries ago, who noticed warmer-than-normal coastal conditions periodically around Christmas time and nicknamed it “El Nino” in reference to the birth of Jesus.

What is La Nina?

Scientists discovered an opposite weather pattern to El Nino in the 1980s and named it La Nina – meaning “little girl” in Spanish.

This natural climate pattern sees surface water in the tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually cool and can last for up to three years.

When did the current El Nino begin?

US meteorologists from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced the beginning of El Nino in June, saying it could last until spring 2027.

The previous El Nino event lasted around 12 months from June 2023 and May 2024.

open image in gallery Adult and immature blue-footed boobies (Sula nebouxii) rest on rocks near the entrance to the Panama Canal as seabirds native to the cold, nutrient-rich waters off Peru and Chile appear outside their usual range while El Nino warms the eastern Pacific. ( Reuters )

It followed the world’s most recent La Nina event, which lasted roughly 31 months from late 2020 to early 2023.

What usually happens during El Nino?

That part of the Pacific where El Nino happens can shift weather patterns across the globe and cause a range of impacts depending on its strength.

These include the risk of heavy rainfall, storms, floods and droughts in certain locations around the world, as well as soaring temperatures.

The extreme weather can devastate crop yields and ecosystems, drive health crises and cause major economic damage.

The last El Nino intensified global heat, drove severe droughts, heavy floods, widespread marine heatwaves and coral bleaching across the world.

It also contributed to 2024 being the hottest year on record globally.

How is this El Nino event different?

Many forecasts suggest that this El Nino will end up being the strongest on record.

Although not a scientific term, media outlets and commentators are calling it a “super El Nino”, which is when sea surface temperatures rise at least 2C above the long-term average.

Last week, NOAA confirmed that temperatures had exceeded this threshold and said El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter 2026-27.

open image in gallery A woman fetches drinking water from an unprotected well, as Zimbabwe is experiencing an El Nino-induced drought. ( Reuters )

The agency said that during the October-December 2026 season, there is a 69% chance of a historic event that would exceed the strength of El Nino events dating back to 1950.

Professor Adam Scaife, head of long-range forecasting at the Met Office, said: “A typical El Nino leads to an equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperature rise of between one to 2C, with 2C being a really big event.

“This implies that if the forecast is accurate – and other forecast systems show similar extreme values – then 2026 will far exceed our recent experience of El Nino and its worldwide climate influences.”

Why could 2027 be the hottest year on record?

Forecasters say this unprecedented El Nino means next year could be the hottest on record.

Dr Nick Dunstone, Met Office science fellow, said: “During large El Nino events significantly more heat is released from the ocean to the atmosphere, leading to an increase in global average temperature, particularly in the calendar year following the winter peak of the El Nino.

“Hence, 2027 is very likely to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record and be another year to temporarily exceed plus 1.5C above the pre-industrial period”.

How is climate change involved?

The relationship between climate change and El Nino events remains an area of scientific research.

Some research suggests that global warming can contribute to making El Nino events more intense.

Burning fossil fuels for energy and transport drives climate change by trapping more and more of the sun’s heat in the atmosphere.

This is leading to cascading effects such as melting ice sheets, warming oceans, biodiversity loss and volatile weather conditions.

open image in gallery Burning fossil fuels drives climate change by trapping more and more of the sun’s heat in the atmosphere. ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

As El Nino adds extra heat to an already-warming planet, the effects of one activity can compound the impacts of the other.

Dr Ella Gilbert, presenter and climate scientist, most recently at the British Antarctic Survey, said the current El Nino will “turbocharge” global temperatures.

“If climate heating is loading the dice towards more extreme events, then El Niño is adding weight,” she said.

How could it affect the UK?

Forecasters have warned that the UK is set to experience more storms and rain in autumn and winter caused by the “unprecedented” El Nino event.

Professor Adam Scaife said: “We should be clear that this is an unprecedented event.

“I have never seen an El Nino signal this intense in our forecasts.”

It comes after the UK experienced a string of heatwaves and shortage of rainfall over the summer, which created the driest July in 190 years and has pushed almost three-quarters (71.3%) of England and all of Wales into drought.

This has put severe pressure on the water system, wildlife, farmers, emergency services and infrastructure.

Professor Stephen Belcher, the Met Office’s chief of science and technology, said: “This summer we have experienced heat waves across Europe reminding us of the effects of climate change, this large El Nino is a reminder that natural variations in the climate system are also at play, adding to the stresses of climate change.”

Canada has vowed to match 50 per cent U.S. tariffs on Canadian products “dollar for dollar” as Donald Trump’s import taxes come into force.

The tariffs, on $20 billion worth of Canadian products, came into force early Saturday after last-minute negotiations failed.

Trump’s tariffs will hit about 5 per cent of what Canada ships to the U.S. every year.

The goods affected range from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney immediately promised to retaliate, saying: “Canada will match those tariffs dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses.”

Canada sought concessions on steel, aluminium, lumber and cars, but the U.S. was unwilling to provide those, a senior official in the Trump administration said.

open image in gallery US President Donald Trump speaks with Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney at the G7 summit earlier this year ( AFP/Getty )

“Tonight, Canada declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week,” U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said shortly before midnight.

“Despite the U.S. offer to Canada to receive the best treatment of any major exporter to our market, new demands and walk-backs of other commitments by Canada have upended the careful balance reached in the past days.”

Carney blamed Washington for the breakdown, saying that “last-minute changes in the U.S. proposed terms were unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal.”

He said that he had suspended negotiations and told Canada’s negotiating team to return to Ottawa.

He added that his government would announce additional support for Canadian workers and businesses in the coming days.

Greer said that the U.S. offer was “forward-looking” and included “a historic economic and national security partnership.”

open image in gallery Trucks passing over Fort Erie's Peace Bridge between Canada and the U.S. ( AFP/Getty )

No further talks have been planned. The breakdown in negotiations marked a sharp reversal from two days earlier, when officials from the two countries sounded as if they were headed toward a compromise.

Carney said Canada’s goal throughout the negotiations had been to secure the best possible agreement, “never a deal at any price or on any deadline.”

The political impact will likely be even bigger than the economic fallout. The countries sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services in 2025.

The tariffs were initially supposed to kick in at 12.01 a.m. Wednesday. Trump extended the deadline for three days to allow talks to continue, but the two countries still could not reach an agreement in time.

Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has also made repeated inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.

Carney said Canada had recognized that “America has changed” and that the two countries would “not return to our old relationship.”

open image in gallery Pete Hoekstra, the U.S. ambassador to Canada, is facing growing calls for his expulsion ( AFP/Getty )

A petition to expel the U.S. ambassador, a Trump ally, from Canada has collected nearly 248,000 signatures since July 21. It accuses Ambassador Pete Hoekstra of having “normalized’’ Trump’s talk of annexing Canada, among other things.

Nearly 72 per cent of Canada’s goods exports went to the United States in 2025.

Candace Laing, president and CEO of the Canadian Chamber of Commerce, called the tariffs “a body blow to North American competitiveness,” warning they would raise costs for Americans while threatening Canadian customers, investment and small businesses.

Trump has made tariffs the centerpiece of his second-term economic agenda. In 2025, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he had overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.

Moving forward, Trump has looked for other legal authority to justify tariffs.

To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50 per cent tariffs on products that account for about 5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.

Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs after their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.

Section 338, which has never been used before to impose tariffs, authorizes the president to slap import taxes of up to 50 per cent on imports from countries that have discriminated against U.S. businesses.

No investigation is required to justify the levies. Nor is there any limit on how long they can stay in place.

The rift comes as the United States, Mexico and Canada are trying to renew a trade agreement that Trump negotiated in his first term and once praised as a triumph. The United States has begun formal talks with Mexico over revamping the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). But talks with Canada have not begun.

“Canada told the Americans in advance that if these tariffs landed, it would stop negotiating and retaliate,'' said Barry Appleton, senior fellow at the Center for International Law at New York Law School.

“The American trade representative said publicly he would not tolerate retaliation. Both sides have now committed themselves in public, which is how escalation stops being a choice.''

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Soaring welfare bill pushes national debt to almost £3tn
News.content:
Britain’s soaring welfare bill forced John Healey to borrow more to balance the books last month.

The gap between tax receipts and spending unexpectedly resulted in a £1.8bn deficit in July, taking the national debt to within a whisker of £3tn.

Economists had predicted the Government would borrow nothing and blamed the deficit on the rising welfare bill.

Figures published by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) this morning show total debt rose to £2.985tn in July.

Benefit payments also climbed by 7.2pc, or £2bn, to £30bn last month.

The Chancellor now faces another tax-raising Budget in October, even as strong receipts from self-employed workers provide some respite.

The ONS also said Mr Healey spent £7.7bn on debt interest in July alone, almost 10pc higher than a year ago.

Ashley Webb, at Capital Economics said: “The weak performance was mainly due higher social payments.”

Monthly borrowing was slightly higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility and markets expected, meaning the Government has borrowed £56.7bn this financial year to plug the gap between tax receipts and public spending.

Julian Jessop, an independent economist and IEA economics fellow, said: “The latest official data highlight the fragility of the public finances as John Healey prepares his first Budget. Government borrowing was £2.3bn above forecast in July, and £0.7bn higher than in the same month a year ago.”

July is traditionally a strong month for receipts from the self-employed, with self-assessed income tax receipts last month coming to £17.1bn, about £1.7bn more than a year earlier.

However, higher inflation triggered by the Iran war means Mr Healey will be forced to use the Budget to find billions of pounds to repair the public finances.

Mr Healey said: “Fiscal discipline is the bedrock of our UK economic stability and national security which is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules, with a buffer against global uncertainties.”

The Resolution Foundation warned that the Chancellor’s headroom against his fiscal rules - self-imposed guardrails to guide public spending - has shrunk from around £24bn in the Spring Statement to less than £8bn today.

The think tank called on the Chancellor to use his first Budget on Oct 28 to put the nation’s finances on a more sustainable path.

Elliott Christensen, senior economist at the Resolution Foundation, said: “The Chancellor’s margin against his fiscal rules is now razor thin.”

News.title: Brook falls agonisingly short of Headingley hundred again as England continue to dominate
News.content:
“Yeah, of course I did,” said Cox, when asked if he was frustrated to miss out on three figures. Cox was caught behind off spinner Ali Usman, but believed he had hit his pad with his bat, not the ball.

“Once I got to fifty, I moved to sixty quickly, and thought ‘there’s a chance here’. Just keep being disciplined, ball by ball. I had it at the back of my mind, thinking you have worked so hard, do not give this opportunity up. That is exactly what I do in county cricket. I get to fifty, see how many runs I need to score, and work down from there.”

Asked if his team-mates were feeling the same emotion, he said: “Oh yeah there is. Every team, every player wants to score Test hundreds. Four of us got fifties, so we were hoping one would kick on, and instead of making it just a hundred, make it 150 or 170.

“I am thrilled. I would have taken it at the start of the Test match. I let myself down a tiny bit, but at the end of the day, you take 70.”

Cox resumed on day two on 23, then was dropped by the bowler Khurram Shahzad on 57. In the course of his innings, he was compared to AB de Villiers by the former England captain Michael Vaughan.

Cox is likely to get a good run across formats. England had hoped to call on Sam Curran for the third Test of this series, but his summer is over due to a groin injury. Curran will undergo surgery on Friday.

It is likely England will be without Curran, Bethell and Tom Banton for September’s white-ball series against Sri Lanka, which should mean greater opportunity for the likes of Cox and Sussex’s James Coles, and could even see a recall for Zak Crawley, who made an assured 81 for Kent against Middlesex on Thursday. Will Jacks is currently sidelined with appendicitis, but is expected to have recovered in time for the series.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez would light up Emirates and make Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard ‘go up a level’, claims Gary Neville
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE has urged Arsenal to go all out to get Julian Alvarez to complete Mikel Arteta’s title-challenging attack.

The Argentine striker has been on the Gunners’ shortlist throughout the window.

But navigating a deal for his services with Atletico Madrid has proven difficult, with Barcelona reported to be his preferred destination.



But Neville told the North London outfit that he could be the difference maker in European competition if they want to go one better than their final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last season.



Neville was on Sky Sports punditry duty for Arsenal‘s 3-0 win in their opener against Coventry City, but he felt something was still missing from the side.

He said: “We think that Alvarez wants to go to Barcelona, but if Arsenal could get Alvarez somehow that is going to light this place up, because then you have a world class striker to go with all the other world class defenders and midfield players.

“They’d become not just Premier League title winners, but you’re then thinking that they can go that extra step and win the Champions League as well.

“He does need that little bit of magic up front that when you don’t play well they’ll go and win a big game for you. Has he got enough of that? I’m not sure.”

Neville’s appreciation for the star extends beyond what he can bring to the team in terms of goals, but to how he can get the best out of his fellow stars.

He explained that the versatile forward could be the key to unlocking the full potential of Martin Odegaard in midfield.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS



The Norwegian technician was awarded man of the match for his performance against Coventry, which saw him score his side’s third to seal the result.

Neville added: “I think that, and I’m being respectful to Havertz and Gyokeres, but if there was an Ian Wright up front for Arsenal who made those little runs all the time, he (Odegaard) would be even better.

“I actually think that if Arsenal were to get an Alvarez, I think he would go up a level himself, because I think that would be perfect for the style of play.”

If Arsenal are to make a final push for the World Cup winner, they have just days left in the window to do so, and will still have to find a way to leapfrog Barca on his list of priorities.

Sports.title: Why Wrexham football shirt sales leapfrog Arsenal and Man City at UK airports revealed
Sports.content:
WREXHAM football shirt sales have leapfrogged Arsenal and Manchester City at the UK’s largest airports group.

The Disney series about the Welsh club co-owned by Hollywood stars Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney has helped shirt sales finish third behind Liverpool and Man United, according to MAG, which owns Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands airports.



Shirt sales at JD Sports outlets across the three were up 19 per cent year-on-year.

Andrew Macmillan, at MAG, which handles 66million passengers a year, said: “It’s not surprising to see multiple Northern teams represented in the Manchester league table.



“The airport serves a catchment of 22million people across the whole of the North.

“It’s also no surprise to see United, City and Liverpool featuring heavily in all parts of the country given their global appeal and recent success.

The rise in Wrexham shirt sales is astonishing and partly reflects the club’s growing domestic fan base.

Especially in the case of Manchester, which is its primary international airport.

“But it also demonstrates how impactful the behind-the-scenes documentary was for the club’s profile, coupled with its A-list ownership.

“That will have driven a high volume of sales with the tens of millions of tourists who use Manchester and Stansted in particular as their gateway to the UK as a whole.”



Wrexham kicked off their Championship campaign with a 1-1 draw against Cardiff City.

They are set to play Watford next.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta gives update on Bruno Guimaraes after star signing is denied Arsenal debut against Coventry with injury
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA gave a positive update on Bruno Guimaraes’ fitness after the Brazilian missed Arsenal’s season opener due to injury.

Guimaraes, who joined Arsenal for £75million this summer, was ruled out of the Gunners’ 3-0 win over Coventry with a groin issue suffered in last week’s Community Shield.



The midfielder was spotted with ice on his leg after being substituted during the victory over Manchester City last Sunday and was unable to be part of the matchday squad against Coventry.

Initial reports had suggested that Guimaraes could be sidelined for up to six weeks with the issue, but Arteta has reassured fans that is not the case.



Asked if his new signing could be out for weeks, Arteta replied: “No, no. We don’t expect that to be weeks at all.

“Let’s see how he evolves this week. He didn’t even want to stop. He wanted to carry on.

“Now we start to understand the character of the player, but I don’t expect that to be a big issue.”

Guimaraes, 28, is expected to play a significant part in Arsenal’s season after his big-money move from Newcastle.

Arsenal have already been forced to dip into the market to sign a new centre-back after losing William Saliba to a back injury.

The Gunners announced the arrival of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on Friday, parading him out on the pitch ahead of kick-off against Coventry.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The defender arrives for a fee of £51m with £4m in potential add-ons and has signed a four-year deal with an option for an additional 12 months.

Asked about the new addition to his back line, Arteta said: “We look to improve and to do what we believe is right for us.

“And understand the players that we already have, the players that can give us an edge and improve us.

“Ezri is certainly a player because we are really, really light in the defensive line. And that was a massive risk to take.”

Despite the absence of Guimaraes, Arsenal started their Premier League campaign with three points as they cruised to a 3-0 victory over Frank Lampard’s Sky Blues.



Goals from Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard fired the Gunners to the top of the table and gave them a perfect start to their title defence.

Sports.title: Three points from Arsenal’s win over Coventry: Could Tzolis change transfer strategy and sub’s snub sparks exit talk
Sports.content:
ARSENAL enjoyed a breezy start to their 2026-27 Premier League season after brushing Coventry aside 3-0.

The Gunners bossed the newly-promoted side from start to finish and went ahead in the 15th minute through Kai Havertz‘s smart finish.



Bukayo Saka tapped home the second just minutes later to put the team in cruise control.

And then Martin Odegaard added gloss to the scoreline as his effort bounced in after wrong-footing keeper Carl Rushworth.



Here are Simon Collings‘ three big takeaways from Arsenal‘s win at the Emirates.

TZOL ABOARD

I’ve got to say, for me, the player of the match was Christos Tzolis, I know Martin Odegaard got the official award, but that was a heck of a home debut from Tzolis.

Particularly when we know the next 10 days or so is going to be all about: are Arsenal going to bring in that new left winger as well?

I think Tzolis has given them some food for thought that maybe he should be the man they should stick with.



ON THE RIGHT TRACK

On the other flank, I thought Bukayo Saka and Ben White were really impressive.

I know those two have had injury problems, particularly over last season.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But we saw what made Arsenal so good three, four years ago in that first title charge under Arteta.

When Saka and White combine, they are really effective, and I think that bodes so well for the future for Arsenal, particularly with Jurrien Timber still being a little while away.



STAY OR GYO?

One interesting point though, and this could easily go under the radar tonight: no Viktor Gyokeres against his old club. He would have loved to be playing in this game.

The Sweden star did not come off the bench at all; he was an unused substitute.

We talk about speculation and what’s going to come next in the transfer window.



I do wonder if there might be a bit of chatter around Gyokeres, particularly when Havertz is playing so well and we know Arsenal would love to add Julian Alvarez to this squad.

Sports.title: EFL star rushed to hospital after playing with chest infection as manager gives health update
Sports.content:
BLACKPOOL defender Jordan Brown was rushed to hospital after playing through a chest infection.

Brown, 25, was subbed off in the first half of the League One opening weekend draw with Wycombe after struggling with an issue.



And manager Ian Evatt has revealed that things got worse in the following days.

Speaking ahead of his side’s clash away to Stockport on Saturday, he said: “He’s had a rough week.



“I don’t really need to share too much of what happened post-game, but it was quite serious.

“A lot more serious than what it first looked when he came off.

“He’d been suffering with a chest infection, I had it as well a few weeks,ago but he had continued to play through.

“That infection had obviously caused some reaction, which left him hospitalised for a period.”

Englishman Brown, who joined Blackpool from Leyton Orient last summer, lasted 40 minutes before getting taken off.

His team were 1-0 down at the time but Evatt is hopeful things are set to keep improving.



He continued: “Thankfully he’s out now, and all of the tests and scans he’s had are clear, but now he’s in the process of building himself back up again to be able to play.

“There’s one or two more tests he needs to tick off, and he’ll have those tomorrow (Saturday).

“Hopefully by the end of next week he’ll be back available. It was pretty scary for a period.”

Evatt admitted that the situation escalated mid-match.

He added: “While the game was happening it was quite serious, so we weren’t privy to the information until after the game.



“It was pretty scary for him and his family, first and foremost. And we must always put them to the forefront of our minds.

“But thankfully now he’s recovering and he’s out of hospital. Things are looking more positive.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reckons Man Utd have a ‘good spine’ as his side launch Premier League title assault
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK reckons Manchester United have a “good spine” as his side launch a Prem title assault.

The Red Devils aim to show they have the backbone to challenge for a first crown since 2013.



Boss Carrick has added central midfielder Youri Tielemans to his spine of goalkeeper Senne Lammens, centre-back Harry Maguire and skipper Bruno Fernandes.

Ahead of Saturday’s Prem opener at Hull, Carrick said: “If you look at all the top teams over the ears, all the great teams, the spine is really strong.



“So we’re conscious of that, and I think we’ve got a good spine right now.

“The foundation of the team is important to be consistent — through one game from start to finish and over a period of time.

“You need that solid foundation through the middle of the team. We are in a good place.”

Carrick has brought in £35million Tielemans, 29, and 22-year-old Andrey Santos in a deal worth £50million.

Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, 22, is set to follow in a £150million midfield rebuild following the departure of Casemiro and a long-term injury to Manuel Ugarte.

United have missed out on main targets as rivals Manchester City splashed out £116million on Elliot Anderson, while Tottenham forked out £85million on West Ham’s Mateus Fernandes.

Carrick added: “We’re delighted with the two that we have brought in.

“Two fantastic players who offer us different things. For the value, we feel we’ve done very well.”

Sports.title: Man City’s Phil Foden enjoys caravan park break with family ahead of season alongside Sun readers on our £9.50 holidays

Sports.title: Former England star slams ‘shambles’ Premier League rules after feature is used during Arsenal vs Coventry
Sports.content:
A FORMER England star has blasted the moment Arsenal star Bukayo Saka was interviewed at half-time.

The Gunners winger had just scored one of the defending Prem champions’ two first-half goals against newly-promoted Coventry City.



But his half-time recovery was interrupted by an interview as the game’s broadcaster Sky Sports pulled him aside for a brief chat.

Premier League rules allow for pre-arranged half-time interviews with players at their club’s discretion.



But clearly not all stars – or fans – are supporters of the televised conversations.

Among them was Aaron Lennon, who was not afraid to voice his opposition to the broadcasting rules that allow the interviews to take place.

The former England and Tottenham Hotspur man spent 19 years in the professional game himself between 2003 and 2022.

But the fuming star, 39, took to X during the second half to write: “Players having to answer questions about the game at half time is a shambles.”

Fans in his replies clearly agreed, with one fan calling the half-time interviews “Americanised rubbish.”

Another commenter added: “Totally agree, a nonsense.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But Saka himself did not seem the slightest bit phased by the questions during his break, which lasted around 30 seconds before he was let go back to the changing rooms.

He answered when asked about his take on the game: “It’s nice to start the first game in the Premier League back at the Emirates with the fans. I think we had a great 45 minutes.

“This is the Arsenal that we want to see this season. I am enjoying the game and looking forward to the second half.”

He added: “We want more. We want to score more goals. That’s the attitude we’re going to come back out with.”



That attitude told as Martin Odegaard added the Gunners’ third just eight minutes into the second half to seal an opening-day win for his side.

He may only be keeping the No 3 spot warm until Jacob Bethell (knee) is fit again but Cox put in a good case to stay in the XI long term with an authoritative half-century at first drop. He was aided by some poor Pakistan bowling but still looked the part.

It may be that Cox's best route into the XI going forward is as wicketkeeper-batter so an impressive next two Tests as well and he could pressure Jamie Smith for that post.

He took two catches at slip on the third and final day in Leeds, including a superb diving effort after the ball had ballooned up off gloveman Smith's thigh.

Joe Root - 9

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad were impressed with Root's return to captaincy

66 from 112 balls

Almost everything Root touched in this Test, on his return to the permanent captaincy, turned to gold, bar his limp shot and even worse review on the second day.

He had batted with his usual brilliance before that and was excellent as captain, having had the fortune of winning the toss and inserting Pakistan under leaden skies.

Root, who largely stood at mid-off to have the ear of his bowlers, showed a ruthless streak by hooking Jofra Archer after two underwhelming overs in the first innings.

His funky field placings, including deploying himself at leg slip at one point, also paid off as England secured just a third win in their last 11 Tests. A fine start to the new era.

Harry Brook - 9

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Harry Brook was heartbreakingly dismissed for 91 on his home ground

91 from 93 balls

If fears over maturity was a reason Brook was overlooked when it came to deciding Ben Stokes' successor as Test skipper, then the vice-captain showed signs of growth in Leeds, with his near-run-a-ball 91 enterprising, of course, but not reckless.

Brook told Sky Sports the morning after that the Headingley pitch meant he did not need to play any "rash shots", something he has been guilty of in the past.

The Yorkshireman could have been caught at slip on one - and if he had questions over his temperament would probably have arisen again - but he made Pakistan pay before heartbreakingly falling in the 90s in a Test on home turf for the second year running.

Dan Lawrence - 8

Image: Dan Lawrence scored a half-century at Headingley - but is he the long-term answer at No 6?

51 from 79 balls

0-0 from one over in second innings

Lawrence had the unenviable - and impossible - task of replacing Stokes in the XI. His part-time spin bowling was only used for one over with the game moving so quickly but his batting starred as he struck nine fours in his fifty, around the odd jittery moment.

A bigger role with the ball may come if Pakistan improve. Only then will we probably know if Lawrence is the right fit in the post-Stokes era or more tinkering is needed.

Sam Curran's injury means Lawrence will probably see out the summer at least.

Jamie Smith - 6

Image: Jamie Smith was excellent with the gloves in Leeds but guilty of a soft dismissal

25 off 42 balls

Smith was faultless behind the stumps but will be annoyed by his avoidable dismissal, ballooning a short ball tamely to midwicket. That said, he was left with the tail and his exit did not make any difference to the result.

If he can get back to scoring the regular runs someone of his talent should and maintain his Headingley standards with the gloves, then there will be no questioning his place.

It not, and Cox continues to flourish, then England could have a big decision to make when Bethell is fit again.

Gus Atkinson - 5

0-40 from 12 overs in first innings

1-11 from eight overs in second innings

Much like fellow seamer Archer, Atkinson looked a little rusty in the first innings. Understandable perhaps considering he had just come off a long run of white-ball cricket - a bit for England and lot for Hundred champions Manchester Super Giants.

And much like Archer, he was better in the second innings, bagging his sole wicket of the game when he cleaned up Mohammad Rizwan to put his side on the brink.

This was a new role for Atkinson to what he has been accustomed to of late, moving from new-ball man to first change as Archer and Ollie Robinson shared the fresh Dukes.

Ollie Robinson - 10

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson took five wickets on day one of the Headingley Test

5-51 from 18 overs in first innings

3-29 from 11 overs in second innings

Simply irresistible. Worries over Robinson's durability may remain - this was his first Test since the opening game of the summer against New Zealand having suffered a niggle - but there is no doubting his skill and control. He has the ball on a string.

The Sussex seamer pinned Azan Awais lbw to the first ball of the match and was a constant menace with his probing line and length and subtle variations and seam movement. He was helped by conditions and a fragile batting line-up but that's taking nothing away from him.

Now, though, he needs to stay fit.

Jofra Archer - 7

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer dismissed Pakistan openers Imam-ul-Haq and Azan Awais in the second innings

23no from 25 balls

0-26 from nine overs in first innings

3-50 from 10.3 overs in second innings

Archer lacked rhythm and was a bit too leg-side in the first innings. However, he got back in the red-ball groove on day three, bowling with a big smile and real snap.

He made light work of Pakistan openers Imam-ul-Haq and Azan to reduce the tourists to 13-2 before picking up the match-clinching wicket of Mohammad Abbas.

Archer will also be pleased with his batting - he struck the game's sole six and added two fours as well to help England take their first-innings lead in excess of 200.

Josh Tongue - 10

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Josh Tongue claimed five wickets during the first day of the Test against Pakistan

5-46 from 9.1 overs in first innings

3-43 from seven overs in second innings

We had the peculiar sight of the ball being cut in half and Tongue and Robinson taking a segment each after their first-innings five-fors and when they both ended up with eight wickets in the Test, it must have made picking player of the match a tough ask.

Robinson took that accolade but we can't split the seamers in our ratings - each get 10 out of 10.

Tongue built on Robinson's early work in Pakistan's first dig, nipping in to break a 91-run third-wicket stand and then scything through the lower middle order, while his three wickets soon after lunch on the third day largely guaranteed we would not have a fourth.

Hailed as England's "best and most valuable bowler" and "a real trump card" by Sky Sports' Stuart Broad, Tongue will have a massive role to play moving forward. He shone in the last Ashes and his success in the next one, in 2027, could be crucial.

Sports.title: 'A massive 10 days' - Neville tells Arsenal to get Alvarez before deadline
Sports.content:
Defending Premier League champions Arsenal would become Champions League winners if they land Julian Alvarez in the final days of the transfer window, says Gary Neville.

The Gunners have made an impressive start to the new campaign, backing up their Community Shield win over Manchester City with a 3-0 demolition of newly-promoted Coventry.

However, Sky Sports pundit Neville says Arsenal still need "a bit of magic up front" and believes Atletico Madrid's Alvarez is the player who would deliver it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry

Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs keen on Argentina international Alvarez, although Atletico CEO Miguel Angel Gil said earlier this summer that they do not want to sell Alvarez and would not even accept £170m for the forward.

Neville has encouraged Arsenal to test Atletico's resolve in a bid to take themselves to the next level.

"What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built," said Neville. "If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you'd have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.

"They wouldn't just become Premier League title winners they'd go the next step and win a Champions League. It's a massive 10 days. He needs a bit of magic up front - someone that can win a game for you when you don't play well."

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Arteta insisted "the main focus has to be to improve our players and the connection between them". He noted how little Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Ben White played together down the right flank last season due to injuries.

However, Neville reckons Odegaard would be even more destructive if he had a striker like Alvarez to target.

"He [Odegaard] is exceptional. If there was an Ian Wright-type player up front for Arsenal who makes those short runs he'd be even better," said Neville.

Image: Arsenal's Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring his side's third goal against Coventry

"As [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres always come to the ball, Odegaard has to play possession rather than playing the slip passes. If Arsenal were to sign Julian Alvarez then he'd go up a level as it would be perfect for the style of play."

Fellow Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher agreed Arsenal still need something special in the attacking areas, although he reckons Odegaard and Saka are showing signs of being able to reach world-class levels.

"I still think Arsenal lack a world-class player in the front four," he said. "About two years ago I thought Saka and Odegaard would make that next step. For whatever reason it's not happened due to injuries or Arsenal not being at their best. Those two were close to getting to the levels shown by Man City and Liverpool players, like [Kevin] De Bruyne and [Erling] Haaland or [Mohamed] Salah and [Sadio] Mane. They took their teams to the title.

"Arsenal won the league without [Saka and Odegaard] doing it. They did it by having a great defence and goalkeeper. But I still think Saka and Odegaard can get back to where they were a couple of years ago."

Carragher added: "The psychological factor of being champions now will take this Arsenal team to another level rather than buying a superstar player."

Analysis: Odegaard and Tzolis rejuvenate Arsenal attack

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Vinicius Jr this, Morgan Rogers that... Arsenal have shown that their transfer window was better than many made out.

Tzolis looks like a gem, a real livewire down the left wing. After a stale opening five minutes on the pitch, he set it alight with two shots and two chances created in the space of four minutes.

It was no surprise to se him strongly involved in the two goals that put this game to bed, winning the ball high up for the first, then crossing for Saka for the second.

But Odegaard's start to the season cannot be overlooked either. He backed up the stunning Community Shield display with a first goal of the season here, equalling his league tally last season that saw him miss 30 matches in all competitions.

In fact, this was just the second time since December 2024 that Saka, Odegaard and Havertz had started together. All three scored against Coventry.

Odegaard is like a new signing. And with three open-play goals, Arsenal look like a new team.

Sports.title: 'Dominant' - Arsenal kick off title defence with thumping Coventry win
Sports.content:
Arsenal made a flying start to their Premier League title defence with a 3-0 thumping of newly-promoted Coventry City in the season opener at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners showed their readiness to go again with an impressive demolition of Man City in the Community Shield last weekend and they sent another statement to their rivals for the crown with this demonstration of dominance.

Coventry's unwanted stat Coventry became the first team to have no touches in the opposition box or make a tackle in the first half of a Premier League game, since Opta started collecting that data in 2007.



They eventually made their first tackle on 69 minutes - when they were 3-0 down.

Once again new signing Christos Tzolis shone. The Greece international notched two assists at the Principality Stadium and was involved in Arsenal's first two goals on his Premier League debut, first winning the ball back for Riccardo Calafiori to tee up Kai Havertz and then sending in the cross Coventry 'keeper Carl Rushworth diverted into Bukayo Saka's path. "What a left-winger Arsenal have got," purred Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher on co-commentary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kai Havertz fires Arsenal in front against Coventry as the Gunners begin their title defence

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka doubles Arsenal's lead

This was a reality check for Coventry on their return to the top flight after 25 years away. They failed to make a tackle in the first half - they could not get near Mikel Arteta's men. It did not get much better for them after the interval, with Martin Odegaard's miscued finish adding a third for Arsenal just four minutes into the second period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Odegaard nets the third for Arsenal

With Ben White, Saka and Odegaard combining brilliantly through the right channel, Tzolis electric on the left, and Havertz looking sharp ahead of some slick midfield play from Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly, Arsenal already look up to speed and formidable.

Where was Guimaraes? New Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes was missing with a thigh injury he picked up in the Community Shield win over Man City.

Their defence was barely tested but Ezri Konsa's pre-match welcome, following his £55m move from Aston Villa, was a reminder they have brought even greater strength and depth to that department, too. Tougher tests are to come, with Aston Villa away and Chelsea at home next on the fixture list, but Arsenal are going to take some stopping.

Coventry, meanwhile, will be relieved they do not have to face Arsenal again until April. They host Hull City next weekend in a fixture which will carry far more significance for their season.

The key moments from the Emirates

5: SHOT! Tzolis shoots over after cutting inside from the left flank.

7: OVER! Saka's shot is deflected over after Tzolis pops up on the right.

8: CLOSE! Tzolis is involved in everything Arsenal do in attack but sends his second shot of the game over after a well-worked short corner.

9: OVER! Declan Rice shoots over from 25 yards as Arsenal make a fast start.

15: GOAL! Tzolis wins the ball off Milan van Ewijk deep in Coventry territory, Calafiori crosses low for Havertz and the striker sweeps in a fine finish to give the Gunners the lead.

23: GOAL! Rice and Odegaard combine in midfield and Saka is perfectly placed to tuck in when Tzolis' cross is diverted into his path by Coventry 'keeper Rushworth.

Image: Havertz celebrates scoring the opening goal with Saka

34: CHANCE! Arsenal work the ball into the Coventry box and White is onto it but sees his shot blocked away. Coventry scrambling.

43: SHOT! Loum Tchaouna's overhead kick from the edge of the box loops onto the roof of the Arsenal net.

45+1: CLOSE! Rice whips a shot beyond the far post after another short corner.

49: GOAL! Odegaard, Saka and White combine through the right channel before the captain's miscued shot deceives Rushworth and adds Arsenal's third.

Image: Odegaard celebrates his goal

53: SAVE! Rushworth tips a curling effort from Lewis-Skelly over the bar for a corner as Arsenal keep their pedal to the metal.

66: SHOT! Tzolis stings Rushworth's palms with a drive from the edge of the box from an Arsenal corner.

90: SAVE! Rushworth is at full stretch to prevent Havertz arrowing in a fourth after some neat footwork from the Arsenal striker.

Arteta: A lot to like and big individual performances

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"There was a lot to like. We were really dominant and flowed with the ball, connecting well with one another. We should have scored more goals.

150 PL wins up for Arteta Mikel Arteta recorded his 150th Premier League victory in charge of Arsenal, and is now one of only five managers to reach 150 wins in fewer than 250 games (249), after Pep Guardiola (204), Jose Mourinho (231), Jurgen Klopp (237), and Alex Ferguson (247).

"Overall the performance was positive with some big individual performances.

"When you talk about connection and chemistry those three [Saka, Odegaard and White] have that. They play so many minutes together in the past but they didn't play much last year due to different situations. Even on the left side with Tzolis you are seeing different dynamics. I was really impressed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title

Arsenal playing with swagger?

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher:

"We'll know in a few weeks if there is a little bit of swagger about them or whether it was just the case they were playing against a team that were not used to that level. But Arsenal showed their class."

Odegaard: We can play even better!

Martin Odegaard speaking to Sky Sports:

"The first game is always a bit nervy. They played well, gave us a good fight and a good battle. Was key to get the first goal and control the game. It was solid.

"We looked good. We could have created and scored more. We can be more precise and sharp around the box. It's a good performance but we can do even better.

"The quality in the squad is unbelievable. You can put anyone on the pitch and they can perform at the highest level. We push one another to get better."

Lampard: A big learning curve

Coventry boss Frank Lampard:

"I didn't mind the reaction towards the end of the game as we went on. I saw some okay things there. It was a big learning curve, I believe they kept going, they kept going much to the end.

"There's Premier League debuts, there's noise here, I remember that [as a player]. It's different to the Championship in a way, no matter where you go.

"So those things are things to handle as a player, and we talked about a lot before the game. They'll have to go through that and experience that."

YOUR VIEWS: Coventry concerns and encouraging signs for Arsenal

Sheldon: Quality of Tzolis!! I know it's a first game back but if he continues like that £34m looks like a bargain, great first performance from the champions COYG!!

Reeze: Arsenal will walk the league this year, even without adding another forward. Problem is, they probably will add another!

Craig: Arsenal looked good and comfortable and never really had to break sweat but I thought Coventry were very, very poor, the goalkeeper has thrown one in and gifted them another. Tonight won't define their season but they are going to have to be much, much better.

Combo: Arsenal played well but Coventry don't look great so it's hard to judge it. We got the goals at decent times and controlled basically everything in the game. Probably could have gotten more but good start to the season. And for Coventry, it will be a real battle this season.

Luca Hill: Tzolis is Arsenal's Kvaratskhelia. A new, underestimated, diamond to the crown.

Sports.title: Wigan top Super League table with win over Wakefield as Leigh rout Bradford
Sports.content:
Wigan eased to the top of the Betfred Super League table with a club-record 12th straight win after seeing off gutsy Wakefield 26-12 at the Brick Community Stadium.

Matt Peet's men brutally exploited a series of handling errors by the visitors to muscle into a 20-point half-time lead, then repelled a fine fightback with Jai Field's length-of-field interception just past the hour mark to seal their win.

The manner and timing of their move into pole position looks ominous for their top-flight rivals, not least long-time leaders Leeds who are now under pressure when they head to York on Sunday.

Peet praised his side's tenacity, saying: "I'm very pleased with how the game unfolded. The first half was intense and went set for set for a long time and we came out the other side of that.

"In the second half we got a little bit sloppy but we had to defend for the most part and it probably did us good. Wakefield throw so much threat at you and they never stop asking questions."

It marked a fourth straight loss for Wakefield, who started well and were aggrieved to be denied the opening try when Oliver Pratt sent Max Jowitt sliding over, but he was ruled to have knocked on in the process of grounding.

Moments earlier, Wakefield rode their luck to stay level after a rare error from Bevan French, who sent Zach Eckersley over in the corner from a forward pass.

Luke Thompson came close for Wigan while Wakefield continued to benefit on the short side as a high-quality contest moved past the quarter-hour without a point on the board.

But Wigan proceeded to capitalise on a pair of Wakefield errors to run in three tries in the next 10 minutes and give themselves an almost insurmountable advantage.

French ruthlessly punished a careless pass by Jowitt by powering over the halfway line to open the scoring, and six minutes later Wigan built on a penalty pass with Kian McDermott's superb ball gifting Liam Marshall the second in the corner.

Marshall was in for his second almost immediately after another handling error gifted Wigan the advantage. Three kicks from Adam Keighran - coupled with a penalty on the hooter - sent Peet's men in at the interval four scores to the good.

Wakefield might have been all but resigned to another defeat but they will take great heart from the way they refused to accept the seemingly inevitable at the start of the second half.

They seized on a sustained spell of pressure to narrow the deficit on 52 minutes when Jake Trueman's clever kick eluded French and gave Corey Hall the chance to touch down.

Trinity pushed again on the back of a penalty and a repeat set, and could have further reduced the deficit but for Hall's foot straying into touch as he flicked the ball back for Jowitt to go over.

The visitors' hopes were finally dashed when a spill from Mike McMeeken sent Jai Field scurrying the length of the field to score Wigan's fourth. A late effort from Wakefield's Ky Rodwell made the final scoreline more respectable.

Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell criticised the officials, saying: "I do think the refereeing department have to ask themselves a couple of questions.

"There's two teams that were top class but there's other parts of the game that weren't. I'll be asking my team to get better from tonight and I think [the officials] should be doing the same."

Leopards continue play-off charge with emphatic rout

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leigh Leopards against Bradford Bulls in the Super League

Leigh Leopards continued their charge for the play-offs with a 62-10 thumping of Bradford Bulls.

Adam Cook scored 30 points, slotting over all 11 kicks and crossing for two tries, with Leigh adding 48 points in a one-sided second half.

Robbie Mulhern scored the first try for the hosts in the 12th minute, with Cook adding the conversion and a penalty before poor handling by the Leopards led to Waqa Blake powering over in the corner for Bradford.

Louis Brogan ended a spell of Leigh pressure by scoring their second try to make it 14-4 at the break, and the tone for the second half was set from the opening moment.

Bradford fumbled the kick-off, allowing Innes Senior to go over in the corner, and the tries arrived thick and fast for the hosts.

Lachlan Lam started and finished a move in the 48th minute before playing in Cook, who chased down his own kick.

Senior then grabbed his second, Umyla Hanley finished off Lam's brilliant long pass and Joe Ofahengaue completed a flowing move with more than 10 minutes still remaining.

Cook then broke away for his second try and Lam finished off a brilliant individual performance with his second, although the final word went to Bradford and Eliot Peposhi.

It was a fourth win in a row for Leigh, who defeated Leeds Rhinos last week, and head coach Adrian Lam told Sky Sports: "Really happy with it, obviously a lot of confidence from last week's win. I thought throughout that second half especially we were unbelievable.

"Cook kicking at 100 per cent certainly helps. He's been under pressure during the season at times but a nice week for him to find his form."

The injury-hit Bulls slumped to the bottom of the table, with head coach Kurt Haggerty saying: "It was a very tough night. We competed for 40 minutes like we have done for the majority of the season.

"We got to a point where we were so many bodies down but some of the [defence] wasn't acceptable that we tossed up in the second half. We won't feel sorry for ourselves, I won't let the group feel sorry for ourselves. We've got three tasty games to go and we'll keep scrapping."
