World.title: Delhi's electric tuktuk boom gets a hacking shock
World.content:
Few sights and sounds are as familiar in Delhi as colourful auto rickshaws and the rhythmic beat of their engines.

The same could be said of the Indian capital's notorious air pollution, fed in part by the three-wheelers' belching exhausts.

Indrajeet Sachdeva has been driving one for decades, earning a few hundred rupees a day.

Now, he says his career is at risk after Delhi's government announced a ban on new non-electric rickshaws from January 2027.

From April 2028, the ban will extend to new motorcycles and scooters as well, slowly replacing more than 6 million small vehicles registered in the city in a bid to clean its persistent smog.

"This policy is like bringing a mongoose to kill a snake. What will we do if the mongoose kills us?" Mr Sachdeva said.

More than 95,000 auto rickshaws are registered in the Delhi National Capital Territory. (ABC News: Bhat Burhan)

Tuktuk no more

Since the 50s, rickshaws with two-stroke engines have become notorious for their iconic tuktuk sound and smoky exhausts, contributing to harmful smog in Delhi and other large Asian cities.

India's Supreme Court mandated Delhi's rickshaws switch to compressed natural gas (CNG) in 2001 to help clean the city's air, but the problem hasn't gone away.

In 2025, air quality tracking service IQAir ranked Delhi's urban area as the most polluted on Earth.

Delhi's toxic smog compared to smoking 50 cigarettes a day Delhi's notorious air pollution kills thousands. Can it be fixed?

"Estimates vary between one-third to 50 per cent [of Delhi's pollution] coming from transport," International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India director Amit Bhatt said.

"We've found that CNG vehicles are not so clean when it comes to nitrogen oxide emissions, and nitrogen oxides lead to secondary particulate matter [in the air]."

Despite the persistent pollution, many rickshaw drivers still consider CNG a clean alternative to petrol and fear losing their income to another change.

"I have been driving an auto since 2002 and [an electric rickshaw] costs 250,000 to 300,000 rupees ($3,700-$4,400)," rickshaw driver Suraj Kumar Gupta said.

" If I buy in this age, I would be tired paying interest on the loan. Either the auto will get old or I will. "

Mr Sachdeva, who leads a welfare group for rickshaw drivers in the city, said they were planning a legal challenge before the restrictions in January.

Electric rickshaw revolution

Sunitha Anup is a researcher at the International Council on Clean Transportation in India. (ABC News: Som Patidar)

Regardless of the challenge, they may soon be outnumbered by others who have already switched.

ICCT researcher Sunitha Anup said their analysis indicated around half of India's rickshaws were already electric, a far higher percentage than any other class of vehicle.

"For four-wheelers, it's around 4 per cent," she said.

Other South and South-East Asian countries have also embraced electric scooters, motorcycles and rickshaws far more than electric cars.

India's micro-EV boom has been partly supported by imported components that can be easily adapted for use by local manufacturers.

However, just days after Delhi's cabinet signed its new EV policy into law, the drivers of those affordable electric rickshaws were given a rude shock.

Battery hacking

In July, videos began to spread online showing electric rickshaws stopping dead on Delhi's streets.

The hack was simple and spread quickly: scammers would download a free battery management app, scan for passing vehicles with unsecured Bluetooth connections, then use the app to disable the battery remotely.

Loading Instagram content

Some would use this opportunity to extort money from the driver.

The Indian government responded quickly, ordering Google and Apple to remove some Chinese battery management apps from app stores.

Experts have warned that many of Delhi's electric rickshaws are still vulnerable.

"These [banned] apps are not the only apps; anybody can write such an app and share it," International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad director Sandeep Kumar Shukla said.

"We have these battery packs being imported and being fitted into vehicles without any cybersecurity compliance check.

" In fact, there is no guideline or compliance requirement [in India] against which it can be checked. "

Incoming surge

As organised and vocal as Delhi's rickshaw drivers may be, they are far outnumbered by the city's motorcycles and scooters.

With the ban on new non-electric two-wheeled vehicles starting in April 2028, the countdown is on to prepare the electrical grid for a surge in charging.

ICCT's Mr Bhatt said the smaller size of two- and three-wheeled EVs would make the transition easier for Delhi's infrastructure but admitted that access to chargers would be an obstacle for many.

Electric rickshaw drivers have reported technical issues at swappable battery charge points in Delhi. (ABC News: Bhat Burhan)

"Two-wheelers and three-wheelers do not require the massive public charging which a truck or a bus or even a car would require; a lot of charging will happen at home," Mr Bhatt said.

However, he conceded that after owning an EV himself for four years in Delhi, he still hadn't been permitted to install a charger at his home.

"My resident welfare association is saying, 'What if it catches fire because there is no [regulation or guidelines] on how to go about setting up this charging?'" he said.

This Delhi public charger listed four batteries as ready but then said none were available when a request was made. (ABC News: Bhat Burhan)

Driver Indrajeet Sachdeva estimated 90 per cent of rickshaw owners did not have a space at home to install chargers.

At one of Delhi's public charging stations for swappable batteries, the ABC watched drivers waiting while the machine's display listed four batteries were ready.

When a battery was requested from the machine, a pop-up message said none were available.

Mr Sachdeva said issues like this meant the government needed to give the industry more time before going all-in on electrification.

Delhi's chief minister's office did not respond to a request for comment.

World.title: Teen hospitalised on NSW Central Coast after alleged stabbing
World.content:
A teenage boy has undergone surgery after he was allegedly stabbed at Terrigal on the NSW Central Coast on Friday night.

Emergency services were called to a home on Painters Lane about 9:45pm, with paramedics treating the 15-year-old for an alleged stab wound, before he was taken to Gosford Hospital in a critical condition.

Officers with Brisbane Water Police District set up a crime scene, with investigations focusing on two groups of teenagers that were reportedly in the area at the time.

"Those two groups met up in the Terrigal area; they appear to have gone to Painters Lane," Brisbane Water Police District, Detective Chief Inspector John Zdrilic said.

"The reason is unclear as to why they did that, and an incident has occurred which has resulted in the [alleged] stabbing of the 15-year-old male.

"The 15-year-old who was [allegedly] stabbed was there with two mates, and they met up with another group that could have numbered up to five."

Detective Chief Inspector Zdrilic said it is believed at this stage that there was no confrontation between the two groups in Painters Lane.

Brisbane Water Police District, Detective Chief Inspector John Zdrilic. (ABC News: Abubakr Sajid)

"[Police are investigating] one, the reason as to why they've gone into Painters Lane and, two, whether there's a previous relationship between these two groups," he said.

"The boy approached a home at Painters Lane to seek help, with residents calling 000.

"It appeared to be a single stab wound to the left side, heavy bleeding. [An] ambulance attended fairly quickly and he was conveyed to Gosford [Hospital]."

Knife warning

Brisbane Water Police District has established a strike force to investigate what led to the alleged stabbing.

Detective Chief Inspector Zdrilic said a weapon has not been found, and investigators are yet to identify a person of interest.

"We're interested in speaking with members of that second group, to assist us with our inquiries," he said.

"Youths walking around the place with knives is not on. We constantly have operations to take knives off the streets.

" One knife out there is one too many, and if you are found in a public place without a lawful reason for a knife, we will take action. "

NSW Police has asked anyone with information, CCTV footage or dash-cam footage from the area to come forward.

World.title: Mundi Mundi offers music fans complimentary day amid improved weather
World.content:
Thousands had to be turned away from the Mundi Mundi Bash outback music festival in Broken Hill after record rainfall turned its campground into a field of mud this week.

But two relatively dry days — and welcome sunshine for the final day — has seen organisers open the gates for hangers-on to come into the festival free of charge.

The Mundi Mundi Bash has continued despite substantial rainfall on the festival site forcing organisers to turn some ticketholders away. (ABC News)

"The sun came out yesterday, it's out again today [and] any of those people who were turned away who are still hanging around Broken Hill, we're going to let them come in today," the event's founder and organiser Greg Donovan told ABC Weekend Breakfast.

Mr Donovan said the event's full program had been fulfilled, including performances from Jessica Mauboy, Troy Cassar Daly and the Teskey Brothers. The final day is set to feature The Whitlams, Baby Animals, John Butler and Jon Stevens.

Around 10,000 ticketholders were able to attend the event, despite many being locked out. (ABC News: Bill Ormonde)

Safety first as region sees a third of its annual rainfall

The Mundi Mundi site saw around 75mm of rainfall over an 11-day period, according to Mr Donovan.

"To put that into context, the rain we've had just over this little period amounts to one-third of the annual rainfall for Broken Hill," he said.

The decision to restrict entry to the campsite was made after many vehicles became bogged in the mud as arrivals were checked in on Monday night.

Cars queue up to enter the flooded Mundi Mundi Bash campsite. (ABC News)

"We had another 2,000 coming the following day, there was just no way the campsite had the ability to take that many more people … 25 to 30 per cent of the campsite became unusable," said Mr Donovan.

He said around 10,000 were still able to see the festival. Around 15,000 people were originally ticketed to enter.

World.title: AFL LIVE: Bootless Richards kicks goal as Dogs lead Dees; Blues revival continues; Pendlebury hammy heartbreak
World.content:
Scott Pendlebury will miss Collingwood’s cutthroat wildcard final next week and could well have played his final match in black and white.

The Magpies revealed on Saturday that the VFL/AFL games-record holder had suffered a hamstring strain in the club’s loss to the Brisbane Lions at the MCG on Friday night, ruling him out for “two to three weeks”.

In a further blow to Collingwood, rugged defender Brayden Maynard strained the MCL in his left knee during a Saturday-morning training session and will also likely miss several weeks.

The Pendlebury injury will leave coach Craig McRae lamenting a decision to play his veteran leader in a match that ultimately had no bearing on their ladder position. Many felt he should have rested the former skipper.

“These are obviously disappointing setbacks for both Scott and Brayden,” Magpies head of football Charlie Gardiner said on Saturday afternoon.

“Scott experienced tightness in the back of his knee during last night’s game. Scans earlier today confirmed a hamstring strain, and we expect Scott to be sidelined for two to three weeks.

“Brayden unfortunately left the track early this morning during a training session, with scans confirming he sustained a grade one MCL strain. This is the same knee but unrelated to his earlier injury.

“These are unfortunate setbacks, especially at this time of year but Scott and Brayden are absolute professionals and will do all they can to get back as quickly as possible.”

World.title: Gollan filly makes flying return to cast shadow over spring features
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Gollan filly makes flying return to cast shadow over spring features Craig Kerry August 22, 2026 — 4:51pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Top Queensland trainer Tony Gollan was not ruling out anything, including the $20 million Everest, for flying filly Pembrey after she dominated the group 2 Silver Shadow Stakes (1200m) under a hands-and-heels ride on Saturday at Randwick. The Magic Night Stakes winner, which then finished 14th in the Golden Slipper from a horror draw, returned in the opening leg of the Princess Series for three-year-old fillies and was never threatened, running 1:08.74 on a soft 5 surface. James McDonald checks out the opposition on the big screen as Pembrey coasts to victory in the Sliver Shadow Stakes. Getty Images James McDonald took her to the lead from gate nine and she kicked clear at the top of the straight, beating Bangkok Hottie by 2½ lengths as McDonald eased her down before the finishing line. Gollan was looking to the next legs of the Princess Series – the Furious (1200m), Tea Rose and Flight Stakes (1600m) – and said he hadn’t thought about striving for a slot in the 1200m Everest on October 17 with the Kia Ora-owned talent. Hong Kong superstar Ka Ying Rising is a $1.50 favourite to win the Everest again. No runners have been confirmed for the race.



“I’ll think about anything with her, but look, I’ll just let the dust settle on this,” Gollan said of the Everest. “My plan has been the Princess Series. I’ve been really keen to get her to 1400, but anything is an option. “Would I want a three-year-old filly to take on the good horse from Hong Kong? Probably not, but the Kia Ora team, they’ll have their opinion on everything as well. “I knew she had improved a lot. I just wanted to see it on race day.” Seven-year-old mare Midnight In Tokyo made it a feature, front-running double for Queensland trainers in the next, holding out Soothsayer in the group 3 Show County Quality (1200m).



Rookie trainer Todd Pollard, a former Brisbane foreman for Annabel Archibald who started his own stable in February, said the group 2 Sheraco Stakes on September 12 at Rosehill could be a next target for Midnight In Tokyo. Prima Bella hits new heights Matt Smith thanked the owners of six-year-old Prima Bella for their patience after the mare fought back late to win the group 3 Toy Show Quality in her first black-type start. The Warwick Farm trainer feared Prima Bella, coming off 1000m benchmark 78 and 88 wins, would be overhauled late in the 1100m race against group 1 performers, but she was the strongest at the finish, beating Stardom by a long head after the Tulloch Lodge mare had hit the lead inside the last 200m. Resuming group 1-winning favourite Apocalyptic came from well back to finish third. Kerrin McEvoy steers Prima Bella to victory on Saturday. Getty Images



Kerrin McEvoy raced Prima Bella outside leader Gatwick and her superior fitness proved telling. Smith was now looking for more stakes targets for Prima Bella, who had overcome setbacks, including a year off with bone chips. “They’ve been very patient,” Smith said of the owners. “We had a few preps there where things weren’t going that great and they could have easily pulled the pin, but I’m glad they stuck with her. “I think when horses get really fit, they can maybe do things they can’t do early in their preparations. You just have to make it run so that the better horses were vulnerable with the weight, and Kerrin rode it beautifully.” Maher camp look to Metropolitan



King Of The Sea surged in betting for the group 1 Metropolitan (2400m) and a stablemate emerged as a possible runner after trainer Ciaron Maher scored a winning double at Randwick. Starting his second preparation in Australia, King Of The Sea cruised to a 1¾-lengths win in the 1600m benchmark 78. Assistant trainer Johann Gerard-Dubord said the Metropolitan and Caulfield Cup were among potential targets for the five-year-old, which was slashed from $15 to $8 (TAB) for the Metropolitan. A race earlier, stablemate Foire De Trone opened the door to a potential Metropolitan run with a gritty 2400m benchmark 74 win over favourite Le Troisir. “We’ve been spacing her runs, and obviously it’s a long way to a Metrop, but we’ll see how she comes through it,” Gerard-Dubord said. “She’s still very wintry, she’s just starting to lose her coat, so you think there’s still a bit more to come, but she’s had a few hard runs on very heavy tracks.”



The win followed news Maher had secured UK prospect Amazing Journey, which will target the $10 million Golden Eagle on October 31 at Randwick. Boniface set for more Randwick tests The Mick Price and Michael Kent jnr yard was eyeing the Kingston Town Stakes (2000m) and $2 million Hill Stakes (1900m) for Boniface after he broke through in Australia in the Premier’s Cup (2000m). A three-time winner in France, the import was luckless last start but was strong late after racing outside the lead in the group 3 on Saturday, beating So You Are by a half-length at his fifth start for the stable. Boniface and Tommy Berry combine to win the Premier’s Cup. Getty Images



Assistant trainer Ben Elam said the Kingston Town and Hill Stakes at Randwick were “a nice program in his own backyard”. “He came over as an entire, now he’s a gelding, and we’ve seen a much better horse this time around,” Elam said. “We’ve seen that on race day as well, being able to relax outside lead without a horse in front of him.” Thompson galloper proves toughness Randwick trainer John Thompson will step Clear Proof up in grade, and possibly further, after he overcame a slow start to score back-to-back city wins.



Carrying 60kg topweight, Clear Proof ($3.60 favourite) was last out of the gates in the 1200m benchmark 72 Midway Handicap before jockey Dylan Gibbons pushed him forward early to sit three wide. Coming off a Canterbury 1250m benchmark 72 win, the five-year-old was then tough late to hold out Isawyou by a half-neck. “He’s going well, but he’s got to be up on pace,” Thompson said. “If he gets back in the field, he just loses concentration. The plan was to lead. “He will run 1400 because I think when he gets in front and is able to dictate, he’s got a high cruising speed, so he runs them into the ground.” In the Highway Handicap, Mrs Goldberg won the 1100m class 2 first-up to give trainer Matt Dunn a 48th victory in the country-only Saturday races.

World.title: Minor premiers Fremantle fall to red-hot Blues ahead of finals
World.content:
NationalWAAFL 2026 Minor premiers Fremantle fall to red-hot Blues ahead of finals Shayne Hope August 22, 2026 — 4:49pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Carlton will march into the AFL wildcard round high on confidence after a stirring 37-point victory over minor premiers Fremantle. The Blues signalled their finals intent in a commanding performance, overcoming an early four-goal deficit in the 18.11 (119) to 12.10 (82) win at Marvel Stadium on Saturday. Jordan Clark, Neil Erasmus and Karl Worner of the Dockers look dejected after losing the final round of the home-and-away season. via Getty Images A blockbuster knockout clash with arch-rivals Collingwood could be next, depending on other results over the weekend. Sam Walsh (31 disposals), Jagga Smith (31) and captain Patrick Cripps (24) were all at the forefront of the Blues’ dominance in the engine room against a lacklustre Fremantle.



Marc Pittonet shone in the ruck, Francis Evans kicked a career-best five goals, and Brodie Kemp and Ben Ainsworth added three each. The win continued Carlton’s remarkable resurgence under Josh Fraser, who has piloted 11 wins and a draw in 14 games since taking the reins as interim coach when the Blues were reeling at 1-8. Sam Walsh kicks a goal for Carlton. Getty Images The 44-year-old was rewarded with the full-time appointment as senior coach this week and celebrated in style with another rousing victory. Fremantle’s fourth loss of the season did not affect their position on top of the ladder but did come at a cost, with key defender Brennan Cox hurting a calf muscle early in the match.



Justin Longmuir rested three of his regulars against the Blues, including leading goal-kicker Jye Amiss, and managed game time for the likes of Andrew Brayshaw, Caleb Serong and Hayden Young. Related Article Live

AFL 2026 AFL LIVE: Bootless Richards kicks goal as Dogs lead Dees; Blues revival continues; Pendlebury hammy heartbreak But he would have a level of concern over the manner of the defeat, with the Dockers comprehensively outplayed by a far more energetic and hungry opponent. It was the biggest score Fremantle have conceded all season, resulting in their heaviest defeat. Young (23 disposals), Serong (23) and Brayshaw (21) battled hard, as did key forward Josh Treacy, who kicked three goals.



Carlton coughed the first four goals but hit back hard in a feisty start that was littered with spotfires, piling on eight of the next nine majors to lead by 11 points at halftime. It was a defensive act that most excited the home fans, who rose as one to applaud Ollie Hollands’ run-down tackle on Dockers agitator Patrick Voss in the goal square. Longmuir delivered some strong words to his players before they were allowed to head to the change room, but the message didn’t have the desired effect. Carlton quickly re-established their dominance after the re-start and were never headed, running away with the result in the final quarter. AAP

World.title: Local couple buys upsizer inner west terrace for $50,000 below reserve
World.content:
PropertyNewsAuctions Local couple buys upsizer inner west terrace for $50,000 below reserve Robyn Willis Updated August 22, 2026 — 4:22pm ,first published 1:01pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A couple celebrating their eighth wedding anniversary paid $2.2 million, $50,000 less than the reserve, for a newly built terrace in Enmore at auction on Saturday. About 25 people gathered in the living area at the rear of the three-bedroom, two-bathroom home at 30 Francis Street as auctioneer James Keenan took bids from the two registered bidders. Bidding opened at $2 million, followed by bids of $50,000 and $25,000. When activity stalled at $2,175,000, the lead bidders were invited to make a further offer of $2.2 million. After a few minutes’ negotiation, they did so and Keenan declared the property on the market. No further bids were offered and the property sold. The property had a guide of $2.2 million and a reserve of $2.25 million.



There is no legal requirement for a vendor’s reserve to be in line with their property’s price guide. The turnkey nature of the property, which included a fully equipped kitchen with wine fridge, was a strong selling point. Peter Rae The successful couple, who have a young daughter, said that as a family, they all had something unexpected in common with their new address. “All our middle names are Francis,” he said. The home was one of three recently completed terraces in a row and the only one with a single-car garage. Records show the terrace next door, which had four bedrooms but no off-street parking, sold last month for $2,235,000.



The new owners were upsizing from a two-bedroom home in Marrickville and liked that the property they had bought was a new build. The underbidders were a young couple from the inner south. The vendors were small-scale developers. Related Article NSW residential property More Sydney properties are being passed in. This is what happens to them Ray White Erskineville agent Ercan Ersan said the turnout for the auction indicated “a bit more energy” was returning to the market. “This is the biggest crowd I have had for a long time,” he said. “There is a bit more confidence from buyers – they are seeing value now.” The turnkey nature of the property also turned buyers’ heads, he said.



“It is so expensive to renovate now. A lot of people are in two-bedroom houses [they want to renovate] but then they get the [building quotes] and they see it is cheaper to sell and buy something that’s finished.” Auctioneer James Keenan raises the hammer as 30 Francis Street sells for $2.2 million, $50,000 below reserve. Peter Rae The property was one of 479 scheduled to go to auction in Sydney this week. In Naremburn, a group of seven vendors sold a property they jointly owned for $2.7 million, $200,000 less than its reserve, on Saturday. Five of the vendors have been living in the five-bedroom property at 22 Park Road, with two others living in Dubbo and Japan, respectively. All were present, in person or on the phone, for the auction.



Three parties registered to bid for the two-storey, five-bedroom home, with two taking part. Bidding opened at $2.5 million and rose in increments of $50,000 and $25,000 before a series of $10,000 bids. The property had a guide of $2.75 million and a reserve of $2.9 million. Related Article Exclusive

Sydney house prices The property premium Sydney families are paying for the right state school Both the successful bidders and the underbidders were families planning to renovate to make the place suitable for their multi-generational needs.



Forsyth Real Estate sales agent Joe Campisi said that it was challenging to manage so many vendors, especially when the bidding stalled. “I was surprised they all agreed to the same price,” he said. “I told them during the week that this would happen [with the lower bid] and then it actually happened, which helped them accept the decision.” The period home in Naremburn sits on a 607-square-metre corner block. The new owners plan to renovate to accommodate three generations of their family. Domain Campisi said that, in general, vendors are now more aligned with buyer expectations. “Owners are becoming more aware of what the market is doing,” he said, “and they are more open to accepting the bid on the day rather than waiting to see what will happen afterwards.”



In Kensington, a young family were the only bidders to register for a three-bedroom apartment, paying $30,000 less than the reserve. Cooley auctioneer Briannan Davis knocked back their bid of $1.1 million to buy 7/22 Villiers Street before entering a bid of $1.25 million on behalf of the vendor. After 40 minutes of negotiating, the bidders raised their offer to $1.29 million and the property sold under auction conditions. It had a guide of $1.2 million and a reserve of $1.32 million. The vendors are moving out of the area and want to upsize.



Belle Property Bondi Junction sales agent Edward Brown described market conditions at present as “normal”. “We don’t have that manic flow of people with FOMO. They are a lot more considered in their buying, but they are still looking for good quality,” he said.

World.title: Labuschagne’s woes continue after Starc’s 22-ball masterclass
World.content:
Updated SportCricketTest cricket Labuschagne’s woes continue after Starc’s 22-ball masterclass Nick Wright Updated August 22, 2026 — 3:03pm ,first published August 22, 2026 — 9:55am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Mackay: Marnus Labuschagne’s hopes of playing a key role in Australia’s looming series in South Africa has suffered another telling blow, despite his side taking complete control of the second Test after Mitchell Starc’s new-ball masterclass rolled Bangladesh for 64. It was in bizarre circumstances that the besieged No.3 was bowled for four, straying across and brushing an attempted leg glance onto his stumps off left-arm quick Shoriful Islam. The 32-year-old has endured a wretched three-and-a-half years, now averaging just 29.69 in Test cricket dating back to the start of 2023, his last century coming in July that year. Marnus Labuschagne’s wretched run of form continues. Getty Images Australian coach Andrew McDonald had warned Labuschagne “needs runs” if he is to retain his spot throughout a gruelling calendar which could include as many as 19 more Tests between now and July – including a three-match series in South Africa beginning in October.



Labuschagne’s dismissal came after Shoriful had also enticed Travis Head to chop onto his stumps for the third time in as many innings this series for 22, while the returning Matt Renshaw – his first appearance in the baggy green for more than three years – caught a leading edge attempting to guide Taskin Amed to the leg side, and was caught at third slip for eight. Loading Steve Smith (six*) and Cameron Green (one*) guided Australia to 3-50 at the tea break. Earlier, Starc’s 43-minute, 22-ball five-wicket haul triggering a drastic Bangladesh collapse in Mackay. Seething from a shock nine-wicket defeat in the opening clash of the two Test series, the 36-year-old Starc’s six-wicket haul began with the first ball of the historic clash at Great Barrier Reef Arena – the 28th time he has made inroads during his first over of an innings.



Mitch Starc has claimed a five-wicket haul in his first 22 balls in Mackay. Getty Images The left-arm quick’s delivery angled in at Shadman Islam’s leg stump, before swinging away to catch the outside edge, with Cameron Green latching onto the catch. Skipper Pat Cummins’ decision to bowl after winning the toss looked better by the over, as Starc struck first ball of his second over as well – Tanzid Hasan (0) unable to dig out a full ball outside off, and instead guiding it off the edge to Beau Webster in the slips. Starc was on a tear. His next ball, he trapped Najmul Hossain Shanton lbw, with the Bangladesh captain’s challenge ultimately deemed to be clipping leg stump based on the umpire’s call. The left-arm spearhead was in a mood to impress the crowd, drawing a low edge from Mominul Haque (nine) in his third over, with Green diving low to his left to claim an impressive catch.



Loading When a vicious Starc bouncer caught Litton Das high on the bat in his fourth over, only for Webster to drop a sitter in the slips, it appeared maybe Bangladesh had some fortune going their way. But that hope was eradicated next ball when Starc trapped him on the pads for a duck, and despite the appeal being turned down, replays confirmed the ball had pitched in line and was hitting to deliver Starc a five-wicket haul in 22 balls. It took nine overs from that point for another breakthrough, Cummins getting one to nip off the seam from off stump into middle to bowl Mushfiqur Rahim for five. After returning from lunch at 6-35, any hopes Bangladesh had of mustering a miracle were quickly snuffed out – Cummins quickly drawing Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s outside edge, caught by Webster, for 11, before Josh Hazlewood claimed his first wicket when Hasan Mahmud guided a leg glance straight to Nathan Lyon at leg gully for 10.



Matt Renshaw and Marnus Labuschagne in Mackay. Getty Images There was one moment of controversy which soon followed, as Taskin Islam skied an attempted slog, only to get in Hazlewood’s way as the towering seamer attempted to get into position to take the catch. The umpires deemed the batter had not intentionally obstructed Hazlewood. Related Article Exclusive

Australian cricket ‘Never let him settle’: Spin legend Mushie on Warne, Lyon and how Bangladesh humbled Australia But his reprieve was short-lived, as the very next over he went for a similar shot off Cummins, only to send it straight down Lyon’s throat. A lavish boundary over backward point off Shoriful helped Bangladesh avoid equalling their lowest-ever Test total of 43, set against the West Indies in 2018, with he and Taijul Islam sharing in a 25- run stand – the highest partnership of the innings – before Starc claimed his sixth scalp, finishing with 6-12, in dismissing the former caught behind by Alex Carey.



Trailing 1-0 in the series, the Australians stepped out in Mackay with the one change – Queensland’s Renshaw replacing Jake Weatherald to open the batting alongside Travis Head. Bangladesh made one change to their triumphant line-up, with left-arm quick Shoriful coming in for Ebadot Hossain. Second Test XIs Australia: Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Beau Webster, Pat Cummins (capt), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood Bangladesh: Tanzid Hasan, Shadman Islam, Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (capt), Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Hasan Mahmud, Taskin Ahmed, Taijul Islam, Shoriful Islam

World.title: ‘Scorched earth for satire’: How this former ambassador’s show was scuppered by Trump
World.content:
Exclusive NationalComedy ‘Scorched earth for satire’: How this former ambassador’s show was scuppered by Trump Stephen Brook August 22, 2026 — 1:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Diplomats never tell, but a new dark TV comedy created by the former Australian ambassador to France promises to be anything but discreet. Brendan Berne, our man in Paris from 2017 to 2020, has just filmed the pilot for a sitcom called Rank, inspired by his two decades of service with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Brendan Berne (left), pictured with French President Emmanuel Macron, is a former ambassador now focused on creative projects. Berne, 56, who resigned from DFAT in 2020 to move to Burgundy in France with his husband and to concentrate on creative projects, describes Rank as “The Thick of It updated for the age of Trump, Truss and Thunberg”. Networks and production houses were interested, but then the US president sued the BBC for defamation and, long story short, corporations shied away from a pointed comedy in the era of Donald Trump, Liz Truss’ short stint as UK prime minister and eco-warrior Greta Thunberg.



“Trump suing the BBC has scorched the earth for political satire, and the joke invigilators and sensitivity readers make transgressive comedy challenging. Five years on, someone laughed it’s been my Odyssey, but I’d say it’s more been the Plodyssey,” Berne says. “When the rights returned to me, I revisited my more provocative scripts, which resonated with investors, and we have just finished shooting the pilot.” As Australia’s ambassador, Berne helped to persuade French President Emmanuel Macron to visit Australia – a first. And in 2017, when Australia’s marriage equality legislation became law, he started a video on social media discussing stronger relations between Australia and France and ended it with him proposing to his Swiss-Australian partner of 11 years, Thomas Marti. Millions in France viewed it on social media, which led to Berne appearing on France’s top TV talk show. Rank is not Berne’s only project. He has helped to develop a cello concerto that tells the largely lost story of a 19th-century French cabin boy being adopted by an Aboriginal tribe on the Cape York Peninsula.



Melissa King, the director of artistic planning for the Sydney Symphony Orchestra (SSO), commissioned the work, by composer Matthew Hindson. It was developed with the support of the Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies and is scheduled to premiere in NAIDOC Week 2028. The concerto will bring to life the largely untold story of 14-year-old Narcisse Pelletier, who was abandoned by his ship’s crew in Far North Queensland in 1858 and adopted by the Uutaalnganu people, with whom he lived for 17 years. The cast of Rank (from left): Phillip Honeywell, Bryan Williams, Felicity Bown, Jodyanne Fletcher Richardson, Dana Blacklake and Will Frazer. “This an important concerto for the SSO, as it brings the story of Narcisse and the Uutaalnganu to a wider audience, the first major cultural project dedicated to this incredible true story,” King says. Berne and French cellist Sebastien Hurtaud, who hails from the same place as Pelletier, travelled last September to the Cape York Peninsula and met members of the Uutaalnganu people, some of whom still had oral accounts of Pelletier passed down from the 19th century. While visiting, Hurtaud played part of the composition for locals.



“They still share stories of the para (white man) who they saved in 1858 and who became part of them. One young woman recounted to me the story of Narcisse killing a crocodile after it had taken a baby, earning the respect of his new community,” Berne says. Pelletier was later returned to France against his wishes, and his parents forced him to undertake an exorcism. Berne (right) and husband Thomas Marti in Paris. “As a former ambassador to France, I believed this forgotten chapter of the France-Australia relationship needed to be told, especially as the Indigenous people were the hero of the story,” Berne says. “I also hoped it might help salve some of the wounds in the immediate wake of the cancellation of the submarine program in a country where culture means a tremendous amount.”



The French embassy in Australia appointed Berne to the French-Australian Culture Exchange Foundation, which is chaired in Melbourne by Myriam Boisbouvier-Wylie. Related Article Foreign relations Trump, subs and the Iran war: Australia’s replacement for Rudd has arrived in DC Berne’s TV program had a circuitous route to existence. In 2022, it was ranked in the top three of a co-production pitching competition, Series Mania, an international TV industry festival staged annually in Lille. In developing the project, he worked with executive producer Glen Condie, the Emmy Award-nominated producer of Top End Wedding. Rank, billed as a comedy of diplomatic proportions, was written by Berne and should appeal to disillusioned Gen Xers. It is set in a fictional South Pacific country, where British diplomats decide to give asylum to a rogue state weapons scientist in a misguided attempt to celebrate women in science week. The team is then thrown into turmoil by the appearance of a bumbling British minister.



The program will be released in December and is available on rankthecomedy.com. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: AFL LIVE: Bootless Richards kicks goal as Dogs lead Dees; Blues revival continues; Pendlebury hammy heartbreak
World.content:
Scott Pendlebury will miss Collingwood’s cutthroat wildcard final next week and could well have played his final match in black and white.

The Magpies revealed on Saturday that the VFL/AFL games-record holder had suffered a hamstring strain in the club’s loss to the Brisbane Lions at the MCG on Friday night, ruling him out for “two to three weeks”.

In a further blow to Collingwood, rugged defender Brayden Maynard strained the MCL in his left knee during a Saturday-morning training session and will also likely miss several weeks.

The Pendlebury injury will leave coach Craig McRae lamenting a decision to play his veteran leader in a match that ultimately had no bearing on their ladder position. Many felt he should have rested the former skipper.

“These are obviously disappointing setbacks for both Scott and Brayden,” Magpies head of football Charlie Gardiner said on Saturday afternoon.

“Scott experienced tightness in the back of his knee during last night’s game. Scans earlier today confirmed a hamstring strain, and we expect Scott to be sidelined for two to three weeks.

“Brayden unfortunately left the track early this morning during a training session, with scans confirming he sustained a grade one MCL strain. This is the same knee but unrelated to his earlier injury.

“These are unfortunate setbacks, especially at this time of year but Scott and Brayden are absolute professionals and will do all they can to get back as quickly as possible.”

World.title: Gollan filly makes flying return to cast shadow over spring features
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Gollan filly makes flying return to cast shadow over spring features Craig Kerry August 22, 2026 — 4:51pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Top Queensland trainer Tony Gollan was not ruling out anything, including the $20 million Everest, for flying filly Pembrey after she dominated the group 2 Silver Shadow Stakes (1200m) under a hands-and-heels ride on Saturday at Randwick. The Magic Night Stakes winner, which then finished 14th in the Golden Slipper from a horror draw, returned in the opening leg of the Princess Series for three-year-old fillies and was never threatened, running 1:08.74 on a soft 5 surface. James McDonald checks out the opposition on the big screen as Pembrey coasts to victory in the Sliver Shadow Stakes. Getty Images James McDonald took her to the lead from gate nine and she kicked clear at the top of the straight, beating Bangkok Hottie by 2½ lengths as McDonald eased her down before the finishing line. Gollan was looking to the next legs of the Princess Series – the Furious (1200m), Tea Rose and Flight Stakes (1600m) – and said he hadn’t thought about striving for a slot in the 1200m Everest on October 17 with the Kia Ora-owned talent. Hong Kong superstar Ka Ying Rising is a $1.50 favourite to win the Everest again. No runners have been confirmed for the race.



“I’ll think about anything with her, but look, I’ll just let the dust settle on this,” Gollan said of the Everest. “My plan has been the Princess Series. I’ve been really keen to get her to 1400, but anything is an option. “Would I want a three-year-old filly to take on the good horse from Hong Kong? Probably not, but the Kia Ora team, they’ll have their opinion on everything as well. “I knew she had improved a lot. I just wanted to see it on race day.” Seven-year-old mare Midnight In Tokyo made it a feature, front-running double for Queensland trainers in the next, holding out Soothsayer in the group 3 Show County Quality (1200m).



Rookie trainer Todd Pollard, a former Brisbane foreman for Annabel Archibald who started his own stable in February, said the group 2 Sheraco Stakes on September 12 at Rosehill could be a next target for Midnight In Tokyo. Prima Bella hits new heights Matt Smith thanked the owners of six-year-old Prima Bella for their patience after the mare fought back late to win the group 3 Toy Show Quality in her first black-type start. The Warwick Farm trainer feared Prima Bella, coming off 1000m benchmark 78 and 88 wins, would be overhauled late in the 1100m race against group 1 performers, but she was the strongest at the finish, beating Stardom by a long head after the Tulloch Lodge mare had hit the lead inside the last 200m. Resuming group 1-winning favourite Apocalyptic came from well back to finish third. Kerrin McEvoy steers Prima Bella to victory on Saturday. Getty Images



Kerrin McEvoy raced Prima Bella outside leader Gatwick and her superior fitness proved telling. Smith was now looking for more stakes targets for Prima Bella, who had overcome setbacks, including a year off with bone chips. “They’ve been very patient,” Smith said of the owners. “We had a few preps there where things weren’t going that great and they could have easily pulled the pin, but I’m glad they stuck with her. “I think when horses get really fit, they can maybe do things they can’t do early in their preparations. You just have to make it run so that the better horses were vulnerable with the weight, and Kerrin rode it beautifully.” Maher camp look to Metropolitan



King Of The Sea surged in betting for the group 1 Metropolitan (2400m) and a stablemate emerged as a possible runner after trainer Ciaron Maher scored a winning double at Randwick. Starting his second preparation in Australia, King Of The Sea cruised to a 1¾-lengths win in the 1600m benchmark 78. Assistant trainer Johann Gerard-Dubord said the Metropolitan and Caulfield Cup were among potential targets for the five-year-old, which was slashed from $15 to $8 (TAB) for the Metropolitan. A race earlier, stablemate Foire De Trone opened the door to a potential Metropolitan run with a gritty 2400m benchmark 74 win over favourite Le Troisir. “We’ve been spacing her runs, and obviously it’s a long way to a Metrop, but we’ll see how she comes through it,” Gerard-Dubord said. “She’s still very wintry, she’s just starting to lose her coat, so you think there’s still a bit more to come, but she’s had a few hard runs on very heavy tracks.”



The win followed news Maher had secured UK prospect Amazing Journey, which will target the $10 million Golden Eagle on October 31 at Randwick. Boniface set for more Randwick tests The Mick Price and Michael Kent jnr yard was eyeing the Kingston Town Stakes (2000m) and $2 million Hill Stakes (1900m) for Boniface after he broke through in Australia in the Premier’s Cup (2000m). A three-time winner in France, the import was luckless last start but was strong late after racing outside the lead in the group 3 on Saturday, beating So You Are by a half-length at his fifth start for the stable. Boniface and Tommy Berry combine to win the Premier’s Cup. Getty Images



Assistant trainer Ben Elam said the Kingston Town and Hill Stakes at Randwick were “a nice program in his own backyard”. “He came over as an entire, now he’s a gelding, and we’ve seen a much better horse this time around,” Elam said. “We’ve seen that on race day as well, being able to relax outside lead without a horse in front of him.” Thompson galloper proves toughness Randwick trainer John Thompson will step Clear Proof up in grade, and possibly further, after he overcame a slow start to score back-to-back city wins.



Carrying 60kg topweight, Clear Proof ($3.60 favourite) was last out of the gates in the 1200m benchmark 72 Midway Handicap before jockey Dylan Gibbons pushed him forward early to sit three wide. Coming off a Canterbury 1250m benchmark 72 win, the five-year-old was then tough late to hold out Isawyou by a half-neck. “He’s going well, but he’s got to be up on pace,” Thompson said. “If he gets back in the field, he just loses concentration. The plan was to lead. “He will run 1400 because I think when he gets in front and is able to dictate, he’s got a high cruising speed, so he runs them into the ground.” In the Highway Handicap, Mrs Goldberg won the 1100m class 2 first-up to give trainer Matt Dunn a 48th victory in the country-only Saturday races.

World.title: Minor premiers Fremantle fall to red-hot Blues ahead of finals
World.content:
NationalWAAFL 2026 Minor premiers Fremantle fall to red-hot Blues ahead of finals Shayne Hope August 22, 2026 — 4:49pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Carlton will march into the AFL wildcard round high on confidence after a stirring 37-point victory over minor premiers Fremantle. The Blues signalled their finals intent in a commanding performance, overcoming an early four-goal deficit in the 18.11 (119) to 12.10 (82) win at Marvel Stadium on Saturday. Jordan Clark, Neil Erasmus and Karl Worner of the Dockers look dejected after losing the final round of the home-and-away season. via Getty Images A blockbuster knockout clash with arch-rivals Collingwood could be next, depending on other results over the weekend. Sam Walsh (31 disposals), Jagga Smith (31) and captain Patrick Cripps (24) were all at the forefront of the Blues’ dominance in the engine room against a lacklustre Fremantle.



Marc Pittonet shone in the ruck, Francis Evans kicked a career-best five goals, and Brodie Kemp and Ben Ainsworth added three each. The win continued Carlton’s remarkable resurgence under Josh Fraser, who has piloted 11 wins and a draw in 14 games since taking the reins as interim coach when the Blues were reeling at 1-8. Sam Walsh kicks a goal for Carlton. Getty Images The 44-year-old was rewarded with the full-time appointment as senior coach this week and celebrated in style with another rousing victory. Fremantle’s fourth loss of the season did not affect their position on top of the ladder but did come at a cost, with key defender Brennan Cox hurting a calf muscle early in the match.



Justin Longmuir rested three of his regulars against the Blues, including leading goal-kicker Jye Amiss, and managed game time for the likes of Andrew Brayshaw, Caleb Serong and Hayden Young. Related Article Live

AFL 2026 AFL LIVE: Bootless Richards kicks goal as Dogs lead Dees; Blues revival continues; Pendlebury hammy heartbreak But he would have a level of concern over the manner of the defeat, with the Dockers comprehensively outplayed by a far more energetic and hungry opponent. It was the biggest score Fremantle have conceded all season, resulting in their heaviest defeat. Young (23 disposals), Serong (23) and Brayshaw (21) battled hard, as did key forward Josh Treacy, who kicked three goals.



Carlton coughed the first four goals but hit back hard in a feisty start that was littered with spotfires, piling on eight of the next nine majors to lead by 11 points at halftime. It was a defensive act that most excited the home fans, who rose as one to applaud Ollie Hollands’ run-down tackle on Dockers agitator Patrick Voss in the goal square. Longmuir delivered some strong words to his players before they were allowed to head to the change room, but the message didn’t have the desired effect. Carlton quickly re-established their dominance after the re-start and were never headed, running away with the result in the final quarter. AAP

Domain Campisi said that, in general, vendors are now more aligned with buyer expectations. “Owners are becoming more aware of what the market is doing,” he said, “and they are more open to accepting the bid on the day rather than waiting to see what will happen afterwards.”



In Kensington, a young family were the only bidders to register for a three-bedroom apartment, paying $30,000 less than the reserve. Cooley auctioneer Briannan Davis knocked back their bid of $1.1 million to buy 7/22 Villiers Street before entering a bid of $1.25 million on behalf of the vendor. After 40 minutes of negotiating, the bidders raised their offer to $1.29 million and the property sold under auction conditions. It had a guide of $1.2 million and a reserve of $1.32 million. The vendors are moving out of the area and want to upsize.



Belle Property Bondi Junction sales agent Edward Brown described market conditions at present as “normal”. “We don’t have that manic flow of people with FOMO. They are a lot more considered in their buying, but they are still looking for good quality,” he said.

World.title: Labuschagne’s woes continue after Starc’s 22-ball masterclass
World.content:
Updated SportCricketTest cricket Labuschagne’s woes continue after Starc’s 22-ball masterclass Nick Wright Updated August 22, 2026 — 3:03pm ,first published August 22, 2026 — 9:55am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Mackay: Marnus Labuschagne’s hopes of playing a key role in Australia’s looming series in South Africa has suffered another telling blow, despite his side taking complete control of the second Test after Mitchell Starc’s new-ball masterclass rolled Bangladesh for 64. It was in bizarre circumstances that the besieged No.3 was bowled for four, straying across and brushing an attempted leg glance onto his stumps off left-arm quick Shoriful Islam. The 32-year-old has endured a wretched three-and-a-half years, now averaging just 29.69 in Test cricket dating back to the start of 2023, his last century coming in July that year. Marnus Labuschagne’s wretched run of form continues. Getty Images Australian coach Andrew McDonald had warned Labuschagne “needs runs” if he is to retain his spot throughout a gruelling calendar which could include as many as 19 more Tests between now and July – including a three-match series in South Africa beginning in October.



Labuschagne’s dismissal came after Shoriful had also enticed Travis Head to chop onto his stumps for the third time in as many innings this series for 22, while the returning Matt Renshaw – his first appearance in the baggy green for more than three years – caught a leading edge attempting to guide Taskin Amed to the leg side, and was caught at third slip for eight. Loading Steve Smith (six*) and Cameron Green (one*) guided Australia to 3-50 at the tea break. Earlier, Starc’s 43-minute, 22-ball five-wicket haul triggering a drastic Bangladesh collapse in Mackay. Seething from a shock nine-wicket defeat in the opening clash of the two Test series, the 36-year-old Starc’s six-wicket haul began with the first ball of the historic clash at Great Barrier Reef Arena – the 28th time he has made inroads during his first over of an innings.



Mitch Starc has claimed a five-wicket haul in his first 22 balls in Mackay. Getty Images The left-arm quick’s delivery angled in at Shadman Islam’s leg stump, before swinging away to catch the outside edge, with Cameron Green latching onto the catch. Skipper Pat Cummins’ decision to bowl after winning the toss looked better by the over, as Starc struck first ball of his second over as well – Tanzid Hasan (0) unable to dig out a full ball outside off, and instead guiding it off the edge to Beau Webster in the slips. Starc was on a tear. His next ball, he trapped Najmul Hossain Shanton lbw, with the Bangladesh captain’s challenge ultimately deemed to be clipping leg stump based on the umpire’s call. The left-arm spearhead was in a mood to impress the crowd, drawing a low edge from Mominul Haque (nine) in his third over, with Green diving low to his left to claim an impressive catch.



Loading When a vicious Starc bouncer caught Litton Das high on the bat in his fourth over, only for Webster to drop a sitter in the slips, it appeared maybe Bangladesh had some fortune going their way. But that hope was eradicated next ball when Starc trapped him on the pads for a duck, and despite the appeal being turned down, replays confirmed the ball had pitched in line and was hitting to deliver Starc a five-wicket haul in 22 balls. It took nine overs from that point for another breakthrough, Cummins getting one to nip off the seam from off stump into middle to bowl Mushfiqur Rahim for five. After returning from lunch at 6-35, any hopes Bangladesh had of mustering a miracle were quickly snuffed out – Cummins quickly drawing Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s outside edge, caught by Webster, for 11, before Josh Hazlewood claimed his first wicket when Hasan Mahmud guided a leg glance straight to Nathan Lyon at leg gully for 10.



Matt Renshaw and Marnus Labuschagne in Mackay. Getty Images There was one moment of controversy which soon followed, as Taskin Islam skied an attempted slog, only to get in Hazlewood’s way as the towering seamer attempted to get into position to take the catch. The umpires deemed the batter had not intentionally obstructed Hazlewood. Related Article Exclusive

Australian cricket ‘Never let him settle’: Spin legend Mushie on Warne, Lyon and how Bangladesh humbled Australia But his reprieve was short-lived, as the very next over he went for a similar shot off Cummins, only to send it straight down Lyon’s throat. A lavish boundary over backward point off Shoriful helped Bangladesh avoid equalling their lowest-ever Test total of 43, set against the West Indies in 2018, with he and Taijul Islam sharing in a 25- run stand – the highest partnership of the innings – before Starc claimed his sixth scalp, finishing with 6-12, in dismissing the former caught behind by Alex Carey.



Trailing 1-0 in the series, the Australians stepped out in Mackay with the one change – Queensland’s Renshaw replacing Jake Weatherald to open the batting alongside Travis Head. Bangladesh made one change to their triumphant line-up, with left-arm quick Shoriful coming in for Ebadot Hossain. Second Test XIs Australia: Travis Head, Matthew Renshaw, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Beau Webster, Pat Cummins (capt), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood Bangladesh: Tanzid Hasan, Shadman Islam, Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (capt), Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Hasan Mahmud, Taskin Ahmed, Taijul Islam, Shoriful Islam

World.title: ‘Scorched earth for satire’: How this former ambassador’s show was scuppered by Trump
World.content:
Exclusive NationalComedy ‘Scorched earth for satire’: How this former ambassador’s show was scuppered by Trump Stephen Brook August 22, 2026 — 1:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Diplomats never tell, but a new dark TV comedy created by the former Australian ambassador to France promises to be anything but discreet. Brendan Berne, our man in Paris from 2017 to 2020, has just filmed the pilot for a sitcom called Rank, inspired by his two decades of service with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Brendan Berne (left), pictured with French President Emmanuel Macron, is a former ambassador now focused on creative projects. Berne, 56, who resigned from DFAT in 2020 to move to Burgundy in France with his husband and to concentrate on creative projects, describes Rank as “The Thick of It updated for the age of Trump, Truss and Thunberg”. Networks and production houses were interested, but then the US president sued the BBC for defamation and, long story short, corporations shied away from a pointed comedy in the era of Donald Trump, Liz Truss’ short stint as UK prime minister and eco-warrior Greta Thunberg.



“Trump suing the BBC has scorched the earth for political satire, and the joke invigilators and sensitivity readers make transgressive comedy challenging. Five years on, someone laughed it’s been my Odyssey, but I’d say it’s more been the Plodyssey,” Berne says. “When the rights returned to me, I revisited my more provocative scripts, which resonated with investors, and we have just finished shooting the pilot.” As Australia’s ambassador, Berne helped to persuade French President Emmanuel Macron to visit Australia – a first. And in 2017, when Australia’s marriage equality legislation became law, he started a video on social media discussing stronger relations between Australia and France and ended it with him proposing to his Swiss-Australian partner of 11 years, Thomas Marti. Millions in France viewed it on social media, which led to Berne appearing on France’s top TV talk show. Rank is not Berne’s only project. He has helped to develop a cello concerto that tells the largely lost story of a 19th-century French cabin boy being adopted by an Aboriginal tribe on the Cape York Peninsula.



Melissa King, the director of artistic planning for the Sydney Symphony Orchestra (SSO), commissioned the work, by composer Matthew Hindson. It was developed with the support of the Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies and is scheduled to premiere in NAIDOC Week 2028. The concerto will bring to life the largely untold story of 14-year-old Narcisse Pelletier, who was abandoned by his ship’s crew in Far North Queensland in 1858 and adopted by the Uutaalnganu people, with whom he lived for 17 years. The cast of Rank (from left): Phillip Honeywell, Bryan Williams, Felicity Bown, Jodyanne Fletcher Richardson, Dana Blacklake and Will Frazer. “This an important concerto for the SSO, as it brings the story of Narcisse and the Uutaalnganu to a wider audience, the first major cultural project dedicated to this incredible true story,” King says. Berne and French cellist Sebastien Hurtaud, who hails from the same place as Pelletier, travelled last September to the Cape York Peninsula and met members of the Uutaalnganu people, some of whom still had oral accounts of Pelletier passed down from the 19th century. While visiting, Hurtaud played part of the composition for locals.



“They still share stories of the para (white man) who they saved in 1858 and who became part of them. One young woman recounted to me the story of Narcisse killing a crocodile after it had taken a baby, earning the respect of his new community,” Berne says. Pelletier was later returned to France against his wishes, and his parents forced him to undertake an exorcism. Berne (right) and husband Thomas Marti in Paris. “As a former ambassador to France, I believed this forgotten chapter of the France-Australia relationship needed to be told, especially as the Indigenous people were the hero of the story,” Berne says. “I also hoped it might help salve some of the wounds in the immediate wake of the cancellation of the submarine program in a country where culture means a tremendous amount.”



The French embassy in Australia appointed Berne to the French-Australian Culture Exchange Foundation, which is chaired in Melbourne by Myriam Boisbouvier-Wylie. Related Article Foreign relations Trump, subs and the Iran war: Australia’s replacement for Rudd has arrived in DC Berne’s TV program had a circuitous route to existence. In 2022, it was ranked in the top three of a co-production pitching competition, Series Mania, an international TV industry festival staged annually in Lille. In developing the project, he worked with executive producer Glen Condie, the Emmy Award-nominated producer of Top End Wedding. Rank, billed as a comedy of diplomatic proportions, was written by Berne and should appeal to disillusioned Gen Xers. It is set in a fictional South Pacific country, where British diplomats decide to give asylum to a rogue state weapons scientist in a misguided attempt to celebrate women in science week. The team is then thrown into turmoil by the appearance of a bumbling British minister.



The program will be released in December and is available on rankthecomedy.com. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.
